summary.text: No. The CPF member must do this personally. A Deputy or Donee may apply to remove contacts if the member loses mental capacity.

details.heading: If the member loses capacity
details.body: A Deputy or Donee may apply to remove existing Trusted Contacts on the CPF member’s behalf.

example_phrasings: Can I appoint a new Trusted Contact or remove existing Trusted Contact on someone’s behalf?
Can someone else change a CPF member’s Trusted Contact?

sources.page_title: Can I appoint a new Trusted Contact or remove existing Trusted Contact on someone’s behalf?

quotes.text: No, Trusted Contact appointments or removal of existing Trusted Contact appointments must be made by the CPF member personally.
However, if the CPF member loses their mental capacity, their Deputy or Donee may apply to remove existing Trusted Contacts on their behalf.
